label: early original-phase steps (t=2-5) of sequences that start with r
explanation: Fires when the first original token is r (24x lift; 97% of activation mass comes from r-initial sequences), on steps t=2..5, mostly in the original phase. The input token at that step does not matter. Strongest at t=3 (56% of mass), then t=4 (32%); weaker at t=2 and t=5. When L is 3 or 4 it also fires weakly on the delimiter step. Never fires at t=0-1, at t>=6, or in the copy phase. The largest activations are all on sequences beginning r r. A weak tail (about 3% of mass) shows up in p-initial sequences and in sequences where r is the second token. Not specific to the token being input.

issues: Minor overclaims about 'never fires': the feature does fire, very rarely, outside the stated window. On dev it fires on 10 copy-phase steps and 70 steps at t=6. Both amounts are negligible (about 0.000 of activation mass).

The misses are numerous by count (13.9k of 65k active steps on test, so step recall is 0.79) but hold only 3.3% of activation mass. Most are tiny activations (0.00-0.17 of max) at t=3-4 in sequences that do not start with r. The p-initial share is only partly selective: first_tok==p & t==3 has precision 0.34 and mass recall 0.016. Many of the rest have r as the second token (o r f, g r c, h r 1, y r q). Adding these drops precision without improving F1, so I treat them as a low-mass tail, which the explanation already admits.

Precision is not uniform across steps for r-initial sequences: t=2 0.80, t=3 1.00, t=4 0.96, t=5 in the original phase only 0.48. Including t=5 lowers precision but raises recall, which is defensible.
Firing at the delimiter step comes entirely from L=3/4 and r-initial sequences (precision 0.92, mass 2.7%; 0 for L>=6). This matches the explanation and is already covered by the t<=4 term.

Confirmed: first_tok=r gives 24x lift and 0.968 of mass. Mass by step is t=3 0.56 and t=4 0.32. The input token is flat (all lifts about 1.1-1.4x). The top activations are all r r sequences. Test scores reproduce exactly (P 0.838, R 0.786, F1 0.811, mass recall 0.967).
